workflowGuide.intro: From the first client to the final payment. See what each module helps you do and jump to what you need now.

clients.purpose: Keep your client's details in one place.
clients.example: A client returns for another job. Use their existing record instead of entering their details again.

work.purpose: Track the job: where, when and how it is going.
work.example: Waiting for the electrical panel? Put the job On Hold. When it arrives, switch back to In Progress.

estimating.purpose: Work out materials and labor before you promise a price.
estimating.example: For an apartment, add cables, fittings and labor. Check the total before completing the estimate.

quotes.purpose: Give the client a price and keep track of their answer.
quotes.example: Email the quote. Once the client confirms, mark it Accepted and you can create the contract or invoice.

contracts.purpose: Put what you agreed with the client in writing.
contracts.example: You agree to rewire a property. Prepare the contract and send it with “Request online signature”. The client signs it on their phone and the contract moves to Signed online on its own.

invoices.purpose: Turn the accepted quote into an invoice and track the money coming in.
invoices.example: The client pays in two installments. Record each payment; the app calculates whether the invoice is partially or fully paid.

jobStatus.purpose: See at a glance how far each job has come, from the request to the payment.
jobStatus.example: The client accepted the quote and you signed the contract: the job shows up on its own at “Contract with Client”. When you set it to In Progress, it moves to “Work in Progress” — nothing else to fill in.

electricCalculator.cosPhiTooltip: Estimated power factor of the loads on this circuit. 0.9 is a typical value for a general three-phase panel with mixed load.
electricCalculator.installMethodTooltip: Determines the cable's current-carrying capacity (Iz) — a cable clipped on the surface dissipates heat better than one in conduit embedded in a wall, so it carries more current at the same cross-section.
electricCalculator.sectionTooltip: Leave on Auto so the tool sizes the circuit for you — picking the smallest standard cross-section that satisfies both the current-carrying capacity (Iz) and the voltage drop (ΔU). Or pick a specific cross-section (e.g. what's on the drum) to check if it's enough.
electricCalculator.trustNote: 100% local calculation, in the browser. No data saved.
electricCalculator.powerError: Enter the load power (kW), a value greater than 0.
electricCalculator.lengthError: Enter the cable run length (m), a value greater than 0.
electricCalculator.rcdPrize: 30 mA, Type A (recommended for socket circuits — protects correctly even with electronic loads present; Type AC is the minimum acceptable).
electricCalculator.rcdIluminat: 30 mA, Type AC (general protection recommended — check if local code requires a dedicated circuit for lighting).
electricCalculator.rcdTrifazat: 300 mA selective at the main panel (fire protection) + 30 mA on each terminal socket circuit fed from this panel.
electricCalculator.pendingSubtitle: Fill in the form and press CALCULATE.
electricCalculator.attentionSubtitle: Passes, but it's borderline — see the reasons below.
electricCalculator.dangerSubtitle: Conditions are not met — insufficient circuit.
electricCalculator.reasonCableInsufficient: {{section}} mm² is not enough: the cable's current-carrying capacity (Iz={{iz}} A) is lower than the calculated current (Ib={{ib}} A) — risk of overheating.
electricCalculator.reasonVoltageDropTooHigh: Voltage drop too high: ΔU={{pct}}% exceeds the {{limit}}% limit for {{label}} circuits.
electricCalculator.reasonNoBreaker: No standard breaker satisfies In≥Ib ({{ib}} A) and In≤Iz ({{iz}} A) for this cross-section — increase the conductor cross-section.
electricCalculator.reasonVoltageDropAttention: Borderline voltage drop: ΔU={{pct}}% of the {{limit}}% limit — any further extension of the run could push it out of spec.
electricCalculator.reasonOversized: Oversized cross-section: {{minimal}} mm² would have been enough — {{section}} mm² is safe, but at extra material cost.
electricCalculator.reasonBeyondRange: The calculated current (Ib={{ib}} A) exceeds what this tool can cover (cross-sections up to 95 mm²) — needs specialist sizing (possibly parallel cables or a cross-section above 95 mm²).
electricCalculator.recommendation: Recommendation: use {{section}} mm² (Iz={{iz}} A, ΔU={{pct}}%, protection {{protection}}).
electricCalculator.disclaimer: Reference values per IEC 60364-5-52 (Cu conductor, PVC insulation, 30°C ambient temperature, WITHOUT correction factors for cable grouping or a different ambient temperature — for runs with several cables together or high ambient temperatures, apply the correction factors from the applicable code/standard before buying materials). Check the result against the applicable code (I7 / IEC 60364) before installation.

online.emptyDesc: There is no infrastructure for active sessions/last-seen (no last_login/last_seen column, no server-side session mechanism — authentication is 100% stateless JWT). Needed: dedicated presence tracking before this tab can show real data.

payments.emptyTitle: Real Stripe data not connected yet
payments.emptyDesc: There is no admin-wide Stripe aggregation endpoint (platform-level invoices/MRR/churn) — stripeController.js currently only exposes per-authenticated-user operations. Needed: a dedicated backend endpoint that queries Stripe at the account level, not per-user.

activity.emptyDesc: There is no activity_log/audit_log table in the database and no event logging on administrative or business actions. Needed: a migration for an audit table plus instrumentation on the relevant actions.

security.emptyDesc: There is no logging of failed logins, 2FA, or a list of active sessions/JWTs (issued JWTs cannot be revoked or listed — no sessions table). Needed: dedicated logging infrastructure and, optionally, server-side sessions for real revocation.

whatChecked.render: Real HTTP request to the backend's own root endpoint, with a 3-second timeout.
whatChecked.neon: Minimal query (SELECT 1) against the PostgreSQL database.
whatChecked.stripe: Authenticated, read-only call to the Stripe API.
whatChecked.smtp2go: Real SMTP handshake/authentication — no test email is sent.
whatChecked.cloudflare: HTTPS request to the public domain, checking for Cloudflare-specific response headers.
whatChecked.porkbun: Access to the Porkbun API for domain management.
whatChecked.github: Access to the GitHub API for this repository.
whatChecked.turnstile: Direct verification of the Turnstile secret key via Cloudflare's official endpoint.
whatChecked.frontend: HTTPS request to the public address of the ElectricalVPF application.

result.notConfigured: No check was performed — the required configuration is missing.

cause.timeout: The check did not receive a response within the allotted time (3 seconds).
cause.networkError: A connection could not be established — the service was not reachable.

cause.cloudflareHeadersNotDetected: The response does not contain Cloudflare-specific headers — the domain does not currently appear to be served through Cloudflare.
cause.invalidSecret: The configured Turnstile secret key was not accepted by Cloudflare.
cause.checkThrew: The check encountered an unexpected error.
cause.generic: The exact cause could not be determined.

diagnostic.title: Login Failed — Diagnostic
diagnostic.networkCause: The backend is not running, is not reachable at the configured address, or the request was blocked by network/CORS.
diagnostic.networkSolutions:
1) Start the local backend (start-dev.bat, or "npm start" in backend/).
2) Check the address in frontend/js/config.js (CONFIG.API_BASE_URL).
3) Open the Network tab in DevTools and check the exact status of the request.
diagnostic.turnstileCause: The security token expired, was already used, or the Turnstile widget failed to load correctly.
diagnostic.turnstileSolutions:
1) Reload the page (F5) and try again.
2) Check whether an ad-blocker/extension is blocking challenges.cloudflare.com.
3) If this keeps happening, check the TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY in backend/.env.
diagnostic.serverErrorCause: The backend hit an unexpected error — possibly the PostgreSQL database is unreachable, or there's a code bug.
diagnostic.serverErrorSolutions:
1) Check the backend's terminal window for the full error message.
2) Check whether the PostgreSQL database is running and reachable.
3) Check backend/.env for correct DB credentials.
diagnostic.unknownCodeCause: Unknown or unexpected error code received from the server.
diagnostic.unknownCodeSolutions:
1) Check the backend's logs for details.
2) Check backend/constants/authCodes.js for the defined codes.
diagnostic.missingTokenLocation: Server → POST /auth/login → HTTP 200 response without a token
diagnostic.missingTokenCause: The server confirmed authentication but didn't include a valid JWT token in the response.
diagnostic.missingTokenSolutions:
1) Check backend/controllers/authController.js#login — it must return { token }.
2) Check JWT_SECRET in backend/.env.

helpContact.intro: Have a question or found a problem? Get in touch — we'll get back to you as fast as we can.

contracts.desc: The agreement with the client: scope of work, value, dates and payment terms. Created from an accepted quote or directly for a client, using a template.
contracts.delivery: Sent is set manually or automatically, after a successful email delivery. Signed online appears on its own when the client signs from the link they received (on-screen signature + email code); the signed PDF reaches both of you. Signed is marked by you, for a contract signed on paper.
contracts.rules: Content is editable only in Draft. States advance in order, with no return. Completed records the conclusion of the contract, not invoice payment. Completed and Canceled allow no further status changes. Custom Contracts follow the same states.

helpWorkflow.intro: A quick look at the states each record moves through, from creation to the end.
helpWorkflow.anytime: From any state, at any time:
helpWorkflow.contractsSoon: The Contracts workflow will be added here in a future version.

clients.desc: A client has no progress states — it stays active for as long as you work with it.

work.desc: The status is changed manually, at any time, in any order — there is no required sequence.

estimating.desc: The internal cost calculation (materials + labor) — the preparation before the Quote sent to the client.
estimating.note: Completed or Canceled = locked. It can no longer be edited or have its status changed.

quotes.desc: The commercial document sent to the client, generated from a completed Estimated Quote.
quotes.note: Sent is only reached after the email to the client is sent successfully — it is not a manual choice. Rejected/Expired can go back to Draft, for a new quote.

invoices.desc: Issued to the client for an Accepted Quote, tracked through to payment.
invoices.note1: Issued is reached by sending the email to the client; Partially Paid/Paid are calculated automatically from recorded payments.
invoices.note2: Overdue is not a separate state — it is a signal calculated automatically when the due date has passed on an Issued or Partially Paid invoice.

jobStatus.desc: The real path of the job, in 11 fixed stages. You don't pick the stage — the app works it out from the documents you already have.
jobStatus.note1: Stages tick themselves off from your documents: an estimate, a quote sent or accepted, a signed contract, an invoice sent, the payment received. The job sits at the furthest stage with proof.
jobStatus.note2: Only two stages are marked by you: Site Visit and Job Closed. A job can only be closed after Payment Received.
